chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkhill (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim said: My father said on the authority of al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, on the authority of 'Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (AS), on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful (AS), that The Messenger of Allah (SAWW) said:

Allah, Exalted be His Sublimity, said: He who interprets My Words on the basis of his own personal opinion does not believe in Me. He who knows Me by comparing Me to My Creation does not know Me. And he who is upon My Religion by using analogy [qiyas] in My Religion is not upon My Religion.

key_terms.الْقِيَاسَ: analogy (qiyas, a method of legal reasoning)

ai.seo_question: What are the three conditions that invalidate true belief in God according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi from al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* underscores the Shia emphasis on *ta'wil* (interpretation) over literalism, warning against imposing human reason (*ra'y*) and analogical deduction (*qiyas*) onto divine attributes. It highlights the danger of *tashbih* (anthropomorphism) by noting that those who liken God to creation fail to truly know Him, a core tenet of Shia theological discourse against the Mu'tazila and Ahl al-Hadith.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 23. Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) said: `Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim said: My father said on the authority of al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, on the authority of `Ali ibn Musa al-Riza (AS) on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefather, on the authority of Commander of the Faithfuly (AS) that The Messenger of Allah (SA) said:

Allah, Exalted be His Sublimity, said: He who interprets My Words on the basis of his own personal opinion does not believe in Me. He who compares Me to My Creation does not believe in Me. And he who uses analogy [qiyas] in religion is not of My Religion.
